maml:description.maml:para: Establishes a connection to the ConnectWise Manage API.
Authenticates and establishes a connection to the ConnectWise Manage API server. Supports three authentication methods: - API Key authentication (recommended for automation)
- Cookie-based authentication (username/password credentials)
- Member impersonation (API keys plus -MemberID: every request is made as that member)

Connection information is stored in the script-scoped $CWMServerConnection variable and used by all subsequent API calls. The connection persists for the duration of the PowerShell session unless explicitly disconnected with Disconnect-CWM.

The connection is only stored once it has been validated. If any step fails (server lookup, impersonation token, cookie login or validation), nothing from the failed attempt is kept. A previous connection to the same server and company stays in place (so a transient failure during -Force does not disconnect you); a previous connection to a different server or company is cleared, and other commands fail until Connect-CWM succeeds.

The function validates the connection by retrieving system information. The server's current API version is read from that response and sent in the Accept header of every later request (application/vnd.connectwise.com+json; version=X.Y), so the module always uses the latest API the server offers. The API version cannot be chosen.

The ConnectWise Manage server hostname. Examples: 'na.myconnectwise.net', 'api-aus.myconnectwise.net', 'connectwise.company.com' Pass only the hostname, optionally with a port ('cw.company.com:8443'). A leading scheme (https://) and everything from the first '/' on are stripped, so a URL pasted from the browser ('https://na.myconnectwise.net/v4_6_release/ConnectWise.aspx?locale=en_US#startscreen') works. Requests always use https. A host part with user info, a query, a fragment or a backslash (the characters '@', '?', '#' or '\' before the first '/') is rejected.
The ConnectWise Manage company identifier (company name/ID used during login). This is the company name shown on the login screen.

The public key component of API key authentication. Used with -PrivateKey for API Key or Impersonation authentication methods. API keys can be generated in ConnectWise Manage under: System > Members > API Keys (or API Members)
The private key component of API key authentication. Used with -PubKey for API Key or Impersonation authentication methods. Keep this value secure - treat it like a password.

The unique identifier for your application or integration, sent in the ClientID header. Register your application at: https://developer.connectwise.com/ClientID (requires a ConnectWise Developer login)

The identifier of the member to impersonate, e.g. 'jsmith'. Used with -PubKey and -PrivateKey. Connect-CWM uses the API keys to request a token for this member (POST /system/members/{MemberID}/tokens) and then sends EVERY request as that member: records are created and changed in the member's name, and the member's security roles decide what is allowed. The connection expires when the token expires; Connect-CWM then connects again. If the token cannot be issued, Connect-CWM fails and no connection is stored.
Changed in 0.5.0: version 0.4.16 accepted -MemberID but silently connected with the API key instead, so requests ran as the API member. Scripts that pass -MemberID now really act as that member.

Forces a new connection even if a valid cached connection exists. By default, a connection to the same server and company, with the same sign-in method (API key, impersonation of the same member, or cookie), is reused without contacting the server. A different server, company, sign-in method or impersonated member always connects again, with or without -Force. Use -Force to refresh the connection or to switch API keys or credentials on the same server and company.
The base API path on the server. Default: 'apis/3.0' Only change this if using a non-standard API endpoint configuration.
Compatibility workaround for ConnectWise-hosted (cloud) instances on PowerShell 7.4 and later.

Some ConnectWise-hosted servers answer create/update requests with an http:// Location header. PowerShell 7.4+ treats any such header as an insecure redirection and throws "Cannot follow an insecure redirection by default", typically after the server has already processed the request (so the record may exist even though an error was shown).

When this switch is set, create/update/delete requests suppress that check AND stop following redirects entirely (-MaximumRedirection 0). A real redirect is therefore never followed, so requests and session cookies are never sent over plain http; instead a genuine redirect response is reported as an error. Read (GET) requests are unaffected.
Has no effect on Windows PowerShell 5.1 or PowerShell 7.0-7.3, which do not perform this check. Can be applied to an existing connection without -Force.

dev:type.maml:name: None. This function does not accept pipeline input.
None. Connection information is stored in script-scoped variable $CWMServerConnection.

maml:alert.maml:para: Connection Lifecycle: - Connections persist for the PowerShell session duration
- Only impersonation connections expire (when the impersonation token expires); API key and

cookie connections are reused until Disconnect-CWM or -Force - A cached connection is reused only for the same server, company, sign-in method and impersonated member; connecting to another tenant replaces it - Cookie-session cookies are marked Secure, so they are only sent over https
- Use Disconnect-CWM to explicitly clear connection
- Use -Force to refresh an existing connection
Security Considerations: - API keys are preferred over username/password for automation
- Store credentials securely (environment variables, secure storage, key vaults)
- Never commit credentials to source control
- Regularly rotate API keys per security policies
ClientID: - Mandatory parameter; sent as the ClientID header on every request
- Register at: https://developer.connectwise.com/ClientID (requires a ConnectWise Developer login)

dev:remarks.maml:para: Connect-CWM -Server $Server -Company $Company -PubKey $PubKey -PrivateKey $PrivateKey -ClientID $ClientID
Connects using API key authentication. This is the recommended method for scripts and automation.
Connect-CWM -Server $Server -Company $Company -Credentials $Credentials -ClientID $ClientID
Connects using traditional username/password credentials stored in a PSCredential object.
Connect-CWM -Server $Server -Company $Company -PubKey $PubKey -PrivateKey $PrivateKey -MemberID $MemberID -ClientID $ClientID
Authenticates with API key and impersonates a specific member. Useful for service accounts that need to perform actions as specific users.
Forces a new connection even if one exists, for example to switch accounts.

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- EXAMPLE 5 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: # Secure credential handling $SecureParams = @{ Server = 'na.myconnectwise.net' Company = 'MyCompany' PubKey = $env:CWM_PUBKEY PrivateKey = $env:CWM_PRIVATEKEY ClientID = 'MyScript' } Connect-CWM @SecureParams

dev:remarks.maml:para: Uses environment variables to avoid hardcoding credentials in scripts.
Connects to a ConnectWise-hosted instance and enables the workaround for the PowerShell 7.4+ "Cannot follow an insecure redirection" error on New-/Update-CWM* commands.

maml:description.maml:para: Disconnects from the ConnectWise Manage API and clears connection information.

Clears the cached connection information stored by Connect-CWM. This removes every connection-related script-scoped variable: - $CWMServerConnection - server details, authentication headers and credentials
- $CWMSession - the web session (and its cookies, including the member hash)
created by cookie authentication (Connect-CWM -Credentials)
Module feature flags detected at import time (for example $CWMSupportsInsecureRedirect) are not connection data and are left in place.
Use this function to: - Explicitly end an API session
- Clear credentials and session cookies from memory for security
- Switch between different ConnectWise Manage accounts or servers
- Clean up before ending a script or session
Calling Disconnect-CWM when nothing is connected is a quiet no-op: it writes a verbose message and no error, so it is safe to call more than once (for example in a finally block).
After calling Disconnect-CWM, you must call Connect-CWM again before making any API calls.

dev:type.maml:name: None. This function does not accept parameters or pipeline input.
None. Removes the script-scoped variables $CWMServerConnection and $CWMSession.

maml:alert.maml:para: Best Practices: - Call Disconnect-CWM at the end of scripts to clean up credentials
- Use in try/finally blocks to ensure cleanup happens
- Not strictly necessary if PowerShell session is ending
- Good practice for long-running sessions or credential rotation
Security Considerations: - Removes credentials and cookie-session data (member hash) from memory
- Recommended when switching between accounts (Connect-CWM -Force also replaces the connection)

dev:remarks.maml:para: Clears the current ConnectWise Manage connection and removes cached credentials.

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- EXAMPLE 2 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: # Disconnect and reconnect to different server Disconnect-CWM Connect-CWM -Server 'different.server.com' -Company 'OtherCompany' -PubKey $pubkey -PrivateKey $privatekey -ClientID $clientId

dev:remarks.maml:para: Disconnects from current server and connects to a different one.

command:example.maml:title: -------------------------- EXAMPLE 3 --------------------------
command:example.dev:code: # Clean disconnect with verbose output Disconnect-CWM -Verbose

dev:remarks.maml:para: Disconnects with verbose output naming each variable removed, or noting that there was no connection to clear.

Companies are the primary customer/vendor records in ConnectWise Manage and are used throughout the system for tickets, contacts, agreements, projects, and more.

maml:description.maml:para: Retrieves all notes on a project ticket in ConnectWise Manage.

Gets the combined notes list for a project ticket from the allNotes endpoint. This is the project-ticket counterpart of Get-CWMTicketAllNote. Supports filtering, sorting, pagination, field selection and counts.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: GET /project/tickets/{parentId}/allNotes
The ID of the project ticket whose notes to retrieve (required). Alias: ticketId
Filter notes using ConnectWise Manage condition syntax. Format: "field operator value" Example: "text contains 'reboot'"
Sort results by specified field and direction. Format: "fieldName asc" or "fieldName desc" Example: "id desc"
Filter results based on child record criteria. Uses same condition syntax as -condition parameter.
Filter results based on custom field values. Format: "caption='FieldName' and value='FieldValue'"
The page number to retrieve (used with -pageSize for pagination).
Number of records to return per page.
Specify which fields to return in the response.
Returns only the count of matching notes.
Retrieve all matching notes by automatically handling pagination.

maml:description.maml:para: Gets the column definitions of a ConnectWise Manage report.
Retrieves the columns available on a ConnectWise Manage report and returns them as a single ordered dictionary of column name -> column definition.

The API returns the column definitions as one or more objects whose properties are the column names. Every property of every returned object is added to the dictionary, in the order the API returned them. If the API returns nothing, the function returns nothing.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: GET /system/reports/{reportName}/columns
The name of the report to get the columns of (as listed by Get-CWMReport).
The name of the report to get the columns of (as listed by Get-CWMReport).

maml:alert.maml:para: The output is a System.Collections.Specialized.OrderedDictionary, so columns keep the order the API returned them in. Use it like a hashtable ($Columns['id'], $Columns.Keys).

maml:description.maml:para: Retrieves service tickets from ConnectWise Manage.
Gets service ticket information from ConnectWise Manage using either direct ID lookup or advanced search capabilities. Supports filtering, pagination, field selection, and custom field queries.
This function automatically selects the appropriate API endpoint: - Uses /service/tickets for direct ID lookup or count requests
- Uses /service/tickets/search for filtered queries
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: /service/tickets
The unique identifier for a specific ticket. When specified, returns only the ticket with this ID. Alias: ticketId
Filter tickets using ConnectWise Manage condition syntax. Format: "field operator value" Operators: =, !=, <, >, <=, >=, contains, like, in Multiple conditions can be combined with 'and' or 'or'
Examples: - "status/name='Open'"
- "summary contains 'password reset'"
- "company/id=123 and priority/id>=3"
- "board/id=1 and status/name='In Progress'"
Sort results by specified field and direction. Format: "fieldName asc" or "fieldName desc" Examples: "id desc", "dateEntered asc", "summary asc"
Filter results based on child record criteria. Uses same condition syntax as -condition parameter. Example: "contact/id=456"
Filter results based on custom field values. Format: "caption='FieldName' and value='FieldValue'" Example: "caption='Environment' and value='Production'"
The page number to retrieve (used with -pageSize for pagination). Default: 1
Number of records to return per page. If not specified, the API's default page size is used. The module does not enforce a maximum; the API applies its own limit.
Specify which fields to return in the response. Reduces response size and improves performance by only returning needed fields. Example: @('id', 'summary', 'status', 'company', 'board')
Returns only the count of matching tickets instead of ticket data. Useful for checking result set size before retrieving full data.
Retrieve all matching tickets by automatically handling pagination. Makes multiple API calls if necessary to retrieve all records. Use with caution on large datasets.
The unique identifier for a specific ticket. When specified, returns only the ticket with this ID. Alias: ticketId
Returns only the count of matching tickets instead of ticket data. Useful for checking result set size before retrieving full data.

- "company/id=123 and priority/id>=3"
- "board/id=1 and status/name='In Progress'"

The page number to retrieve (used with -pageSize for pagination). Default: 1
Number of records to return per page. If not specified, the API's default page size is used. The module does not enforce a maximum; the API applies its own limit.
Specify which fields to return in the response. Reduces response size and improves performance by only returning needed fields. Example: @('id', 'summary', 'status', 'company', 'board')

Performance: - More efficient than manual pagination

maml:description.maml:para: Generic GET request handler for retrieving ConnectWise Manage records.
Master function for all GET operations in the module. Handles direct ID lookups, counting, filtering, sorting, field selection, and pagination.

Used by the Get-CWM* functions (Get-CWMCompany, etc.) to retrieve data. Get-CWMTicket uses it for id and count lookups and sends list queries to Invoke-CWMSearchMaster. Automatically routes to Invoke-CWMAllResult when -all switch is used.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: GET {Endpoint}
Hashtable containing query parameters: - id: Direct ID lookup
- condition: Filter string
- orderBy: Sort specification
- childConditions: Filter on child records
- customFieldConditions: Filter on custom fields
- page, pageSize: Pagination
- pageId: Record id to start forward-only pagination from (sent as &pageId=)
- fields: Field selection array
- all: Switch to retrieve all pages
- count: Switch to return count only.
Must be a SwitchParameter (as in $PSBoundParameters); count = $true is ignored because the check uses .IsPresent
The id is read from $Arguments.id only; variables in the caller's scope are never used.
The API endpoint path (e.g., '/service/tickets', '/company/companies')

maml:description.maml:para: Generic POST-based search handler for complex queries.
Master function for POST-based search operations. Used when GET endpoints don't support complex queries or when the query string would be too long for a GET request.
The filter parameters go in the JSON request body, allowing for more complex filtering than standard GET requests. Field selection and paging go in the query string.

maml:description.maml:para: Generic PATCH request handler for updating ConnectWise Manage records.
Master function for all update (PATCH) operations in the module. Implements RFC 6902 JSON Patch standard for updating records.
Used by all Update-CWM* functions (Update-CWMTicket, Update-CWMCompany, etc.). Constructs patch operation array and submits to the API.

Two modes: - Bulk: when $Arguments contains PatchOperations, those operations are the whole request body and Operation/Path/Value are ignored. Several fields can be changed in one request. - Single: otherwise one operation is built from Operation, Path and Value. Value is optional for 'remove'. For 'add' and 'replace' a Value key is required (it may be $null), so a forgotten -Value is an error instead of silently sending null.
In both modes: - 'value' is left out of 'remove' operations.
- A value wrapped in a PSObject (for example an array returned from a function) is unwrapped, so

Windows PowerShell 5.1 does not serialize it as {"value":[...],"Count":n}. A PSCustomObject (for example $Ticket.board from Get-CWMTicket), or an array of them, is sent with all its properties. - Verbose and -WhatIf output masks secrets: values of keys such as password or token, and the value of an operation whose path is such a key. - The body is always a JSON array, even with a single operation.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: PATCH {Endpoint}

Hashtable (usually $PSBoundParameters) containing either: - PatchOperations: Array of operations, each a hashtable or PSCustomObject with op, path and (except for 'remove') value. A 'from' member is passed through for 'move' and 'copy'. or: - Operation: 'add', 'replace', or 'remove'
- Path: Field path to modify
- Value: New value (not needed for 'remove'; required, but may be $null, for 'add' and 'replace')
The API endpoint path (e.g., '/service/tickets/123', '/company/companies/250')

maml:description.maml:para: Low-level HTTP request handler for all ConnectWise Manage API calls.

Core function that handles all HTTP requests to the ConnectWise Manage API. Manages authentication headers, connection state, error handling, and automatic retry of transient failures that are safe to repeat.

This is the foundation function used by all other Invoke-CWM*Master functions. It should rarely be called directly - use the higher-level master functions instead. Behaves the same on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
Key Features: - Validates connection state ($CWMServerConnection)
- Adds authentication headers automatically
- Handles URI formatting corrections
- Retries 429 (any method) and 502/503/504 (GET/HEAD and read-only searches) with Retry-After or exponential backoff
- Provides detailed error messages with troubleshooting hints
- Records the server's api-current-version response header

Hashtable of arguments to pass to Invoke-WebRequest. Should include: Uri, Method, and optionally Body, Headers, ContentType The API version is not set per request: the Accept header from Connect-CWM (the server's current version) is used for every call. The hashtable is copied, so the caller's hashtable (and its Headers) is not modified. ReadOnly = $true marks a POST that only reads (a /search endpoint), so it is retried like a GET. The key is not sent to Invoke-WebRequest. A WebSession in the hashtable is used instead of the connection's session.

Maximum number of retry attempts. Default: 5 Only 429 Too Many Requests (any method) and 502/503/504 on GET/HEAD (or a request with ReadOnly = $true) are retried. Writes that fail with a 5xx are never retried, because the change may already have been applied and repeating it could create a duplicate. The wait is the server's Retry-After when present, otherwise 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 seconds (capped at 60 seconds).

The wait is the server's Retry-After when present, otherwise 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 seconds (capped at 60 seconds).

maml:alert.maml:para: Internal Function: - Called by all Invoke-CWM*Master functions
- Manages retry logic with exponential backoff

Insecure redirection (PowerShell 7.4+): - When connected with Connect-CWM -AllowInsecureRedirect, non-GET requests are sent with -AllowInsecureRedirect -MaximumRedirection 0 (redirects are never followed), and GET requests with -MaximumRedirection 50 (the default, re-applied because the setting persists on a shared session). - A caller-supplied non-zero MaximumRedirection disables the workaround for that call.
Error Handling: - Validates connection state before requests
- Retries only transient failures that are safe to repeat (see MaxRetry)
- The parsed error body is kept in $script:ErrBody and the raw ErrorDetails in $script:ErrDetails

maml:description.maml:para: Adds an allowed value to a question on a configuration TYPE.

Creates a new predefined value (for example a dropdown option) on a question of a configuration type. This changes the configuration type's definition, so the new option is offered on every configuration of that type.
This function does NOT answer a question on a specific configuration. To set a configuration's answer, use Update-CWMCompanyConfiguration and replace its 'questions' (see the examples).
The IDs map onto the URL like this: /company/configurations/types/{grandparentId}/questions/{parentId}/values
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: POST /company/configurations/types/{typeId}/questions/{questionId}/values
The ID of the configuration TYPE that owns the question (alias: typeId). This is not a configuration ID.
The ID of the question on that configuration type (alias: questionId).

Reference to the configuration type. Format: @{ id = 12 }
Whether this value is the question's default.
Whether this value is inactive.
Reference to the question. Format: @{ id = 431 }
The text of the allowed value (1-1000 characters).
Metadata hashtable passed through to the API as-is.

maml:description.maml:para: Creates a service template for a company in ConnectWise Manage.
Creates a company service (ticket) template.

If -company is not specified, it is set to @{ id = <parentId> }. PR #82 reported that without a company in the body the API returns a record with id 0 and creates nothing. The caller's $PSBoundParameters is not modified.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: POST /company/companies/{parentId}/serviceTemplates
The ID of the company (required). Alias: companyId

maml:description.maml:para: Uploads a document or links a URL to a ConnectWise Manage record.
Creates a document attached to a record (ticket, company, project, ...). Either uploads a local file (-FilePath) or links a URL (-URL).

The request is sent as multipart/form-data. The body is built as a byte array: the form fields and part headers are UTF-8 text and the file content is copied byte for byte, so binary files upload unchanged on both Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: POST /system/documents
The type of record to attach the document to, e.g. 'Ticket', 'Company' or 'Project'.
The ID of the record to attach the document to.
The title of the document. Line breaks are replaced with a space.
A URL to link instead of uploading a file.
Whether the document is private. Default: $true
Whether the document is read-only. Default: $false
Whether the document is an avatar image. Default: $false
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The type of record to attach the document to, e.g. 'Ticket', 'Company' or 'Project'.
The ID of the record to attach the document to.
The title of the document. Line breaks are replaced with a space.
Path to the local file to upload. Must be a file, not a folder.
The file name to send to ConnectWise Manage. Defaults to the name of -FilePath. Double quotes, carriage returns and line feeds are replaced with '_'.
Whether the document is private. Default: $true
Whether the document is read-only. Default: $false
Whether the document is an avatar image. Default: $false

maml:description.maml:para: Bundles or merges child tickets into a parent service ticket.
Combines one or more service tickets with a parent ticket, using one of the two ConnectWise Manage ticket-combining operations:

- Bundle: attaches the child tickets to the parent. The children stay as separate tickets, linked to the parent (their parentTicketId is set), and are closed when the parent is closed. Calls: POST /service/tickets/{parentId}/attachChildren Body: { "childTicketIds": [ ... ] }

- Merge: absorbs the child tickets into the parent. The merged tickets are set to the status you supply (usually a closed status on their board). Calls: POST /service/tickets/{parentId}/merge Body: { "mergeTicketIds": [ ... ], "status": { "id": ..., "name": ..., "sort": ..., "_info": { ... } } }
The request is sent through Invoke-CWMNewMaster, which serializes the body with enough depth that the nested status object (including _info) stays a JSON object.
The API rejects invalid combinations with a descriptive error, for example when the supplied parent is itself a child of another ticket.
Unbundling: to detach bundled child tickets from the parent again, use Remove-CWMTicketChild (POST /service/tickets/{parentId}/detachChildren).
The ID of the parent ticket that the child tickets are bundled into or merged into. Required.
One or more IDs of the tickets to bundle or merge into the parent ticket. Required.
Merge only. The ID of the status that the merged child tickets are set to. Required for a merge. The status must be valid on the child tickets' board. Find status IDs with Get-CWMBoardStatus.
Merge only. Optional name of the status given in -StatusID. Sent as status.name.
Merge only. Optional sort order of the status. Sent as status.sort.
Merge only. Optional _info hashtable for the status reference. Sent as status._info, as a nested JSON object.
The operation to perform. Required. - 'Bundle' attaches the children to the parent (attachChildren).
- 'Merge' merges the children into the parent (merge); also requires -StatusID.

maml:description.maml:para: Deletes a company from ConnectWise Manage.
Permanently removes a company record by ID. This action cannot be undone.

ConnectWise Manage decides what happens to related records (contacts, tickets, agreements, projects) and may refuse the delete. Consider marking the company as inactive instead of deleting it to preserve history.
ConfirmImpact is Medium, so with the default $ConfirmPreference (High) there is no confirmation prompt: the company is deleted immediately. Use -Confirm to be prompted or -WhatIf to preview.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: DELETE /company/companies/{id}
The company ID to delete (required). Alias: companyId
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.

maml:alert.maml:para: Important: - This action is permanent and cannot be undone
- ConnectWise Manage may reject the delete when related records exist
- Consider using an inactive status instead of deletion

Alternative to Deletion: Mark the company inactive instead. Status IDs differ per instance, so look the ID up first: $Inactive = Get-CWMCompanyStatus -condition "inactiveFlag=true" | Select-Object -First 1 Update-CWMCompany -id 250 -Operation 'replace' -Path 'status' -Value @{ id = $Inactive.id }

maml:description.maml:para: Deletes a service ticket from ConnectWise Manage.
Permanently removes a service ticket by ID. This action cannot be undone.

ConnectWise Manage decides what happens to related records (notes, time entries, configurations) and may refuse the delete, for example when time has been entered. Consider closing tickets instead of deleting them to preserve history.
ConfirmImpact is Medium, so with the default $ConfirmPreference (High) there is no confirmation prompt: the ticket is deleted immediately. Use -Confirm to be prompted or -WhatIf to preview.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: DELETE /service/tickets/{id}

maml:alert.maml:para: Important: - This action is permanent and cannot be undone
- ConnectWise Manage may reject the delete (for example when time entries exist)
- Consider closing tickets instead to preserve history

Alternative to Deletion: Instead of deleting, move the ticket to a closed status on its board: $Closed = Get-CWMBoardStatus -serviceBoardId 1 -condition "closedStatus=true" | Select-Object -First 1 Update-CWMTicket -id 123 -Operation 'replace' -Path 'status' -Value @{ id = $Closed.id }

maml:description.maml:para: Detaches (unbundles) child tickets from a parent service ticket.
Reverses a bundle made with New-CWMTicketChild -OperationType Bundle: the child tickets are detached from the parent and become independent tickets again.
Calls: POST /service/tickets/{parentId}/detachChildren Body: { "childTicketIds": [ ... ] }

The endpoint is a POST (not a DELETE), so the request is sent through Invoke-CWMNewMaster. It takes the same TicketBundle body as attachChildren. The API has no endpoint that reverses a merge (New-CWMTicketChild -OperationType Merge).

maml:description.maml:para: Updates an allowed value of a question on a configuration TYPE.

Edits one of the predefined values (for example a dropdown option) that a question on a configuration type offers. This changes the configuration type's definition, so it affects every configuration of that type.

This function does NOT set the answer to a question on a specific configuration. Passing a configuration ID or an answer ID as -id results in a 404, because those IDs do not exist under this endpoint. To set a configuration's answer, use Update-CWMCompanyConfiguration and replace its 'questions' (see the examples).
The IDs map onto the URL like this: /company/configurations/types/{grandparentId}/questions/{parentId}/values/{id}
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: PATCH /company/configurations/types/{typeId}/questions/{questionId}/values/{valueId}
The ID of the configuration TYPE that owns the question (alias: typeId). This is not a configuration ID.
The ID of the question on that configuration type (alias: questionId).

The patch operation: 'add', 'replace' or 'remove'.
The property of the value to change, for example 'value', 'defaultFlag' or 'inactiveFlag'.

maml:description.maml:para: Updates an existing service ticket in ConnectWise Manage using patch operations.
Modifies ticket properties using JSON Patch operations (add, replace, remove). This follows the RFC 6902 JSON Patch standard used by ConnectWise Manage API.
Use -Operation, -Path and -Value for one change, or -PatchOperations for several changes in one request.
This function calls the ConnectWise Manage API endpoint: PATCH /service/tickets/{id}
The ticket ID to update (required). Alias: ticketId
The patch operation to perform (required). Valid values: 'add', 'replace', 'remove' - replace: Modifies an existing field value
- add: Adds a value to an array or creates a field
- remove: Removes a field value
The field path to modify (required). Examples: 'status', 'summary', 'priority', 'owner' For nested fields use slash notation: 'customFields/0/value'

The new value for the field (required for 'add' and 'replace'; not needed for 'remove'). Use -Value $null to set a field to null. Type depends on the field being updated: - References (status, priority, etc.): @{ id = 123 }
- Strings: "text value"
- Numbers: 42
- Booleans: $true or $false
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
The ticket ID to update (required). Alias: ticketId
Several patch operations to apply in one request. Each is a hashtable or PSCustomObject with op, path and (except for 'remove') value. 'value' is left out of 'remove' operations.
Shows what would happen if the cmdlet runs. The cmdlet is not run.
Prompts you for confirmation before running the cmdlet.
